summary: Created so lipsync leaves MPI-4's umbrella and can start. Scope is BENCH AUTHORING ONLY: author and prove the graph on 8188, app integration follows as its own Flow card. Deliberately maturity=planned, not blocked - MPI-531 gates authoring a Flow's app-side UI, not authoring a ComfyUI graph, so this can proceed in parallel. The corrected analysis it starts from is in MPI-4's brief: lipdub is a fourth front end, not a third mask polarity, and everything it needs is already installed.

Implementation started. Bench authoring of the LTX 2.3 lipdub graph: the bench template is read (36 nodes / 49 links), every node type and the ic-lora-lipdub-0.9 LoRA are present on both 8188 and 48188, and plan.md is now written with five phases. It carries one correction to the brief: the audio latent is EMPTY (LTXVEmptyLatentAudio feeds LTXVConcatAVLatent), so the words come from the prompt text and the source audio enters only as speaker-identity ref tokens - swapping that socket swaps the VOICE, not the content. The unused frozen_audio output (noise_mask=0) is the one-link swap that makes the graph audio-driven, so both modes live in one file.
Derived 5 items from the five plan.md phase titles.

Four runs on bench 8188, all status success with 0 node_errors, and NOT ONE moved the mouth. Phase 1 passed cleanly (repo copy byte-identical to the bench, 31 API nodes, 0 missing required / 0 dangling), but two loader substitutions are mandatory - the template names a bf16 transformer and a heretic-fp8 Gemma that do not exist here, so it has never run on this install as written. Drift, the risk the card was written around, did not materialise: 36.1 dB PSNR against the source, identity and lighting intact. The IC-LoRA is applying (37.5 dB between strength 1.0 and 0.0) but its effect is diffuse over the whole subject rather than localised at the mouth. Lightricks README settles what the feature is: text-driven dubbing/rephrasing, where supplied audio is a VOICE reference and frozen_audio is a stage-2 device for the upscale pass - so run 2 misused it, and both this brief and MPI-4 describe the audio front end wrongly. Source framing is ruled out (run 4 gave a head-and-shoulders face at native 960x544). Two suspects remain: the checkpoint (the LoRA is published against ltx-2.3-22b-dev, absent from this machine; we run an int8_convrot distilled-1.1) and the missing stage 2.

IT WORKS, and the variable was face size. Six runs on bench 8188, all status success with 0 node_errors. Runs 1-3 fed a 1920x1088 clip that ResizeImageMaskNode squeezed to 960x544, leaving the head small, and nothing moved. Run 4 fed a head-and-shoulders crop already at 960x544 - same graph, same weights, same seed - and the lips moved with a voice cloned from the supplied reference, confirmed by Fabio watching it. An earlier note here called run 4 motionless; that was a sampling error from twelve late frames while the subject is in profile, and it is corrected in place. Runs 4 and 6 are one link apart and settle the mechanism: with the empty audio latent the model GENERATES the speech from the prompt text and the lips follow it, while with frozen_audio the supplied track is preserved and the lips do not move at all - so the lips follow the audio the model makes, and true audio-preserving lipsync is not available from this IC-LoRA. Supply-an-audio-file therefore needs a speech-to-text step in front, and no Whisper node is installed. Also ported Lightricks official two-stage workflow onto our weights entirely in API format (11 links rewired, dev checkpoint and distilled LoRA replaced by UNETLoader/DualCLIPLoader/VAELoader/VAELoaderKJ) and RAN it: 283s, 1920x1088, clean.

Judged by Fabio. refvoice_tiny_00001_ ("I should leave now.") has GOOD lip sync; refvoice_short_00001_ ("I don't know what is going on.") does not, on the same 3.04s clip. Both fed the reference voice through a SEPARATE LoadAudio rather than the source clip track, so the reference is decoupled from the video and one voice can be reused across clips - the consistency use case works. The sync lever is how much speech the line asks for against the clip duration, which makes it a UI constraint rather than a tuning knob.

REFRAME from Fabio at close-out: he has already tested BOTH reference audio and direct audio and both WORK - on text-to-video and image-to-video, not through the lipdub graph - and he has driven two voices in one audio file for two characters. The only reason it does not do video-to-video is that graph has no video input. This matches the architecture: ltx_i2v_t2v_template.json runs Input_Audio through LTXVAudioVAEEncode, SetLatentNoiseMask and LTXVConcatAVLatent with NO full-video IC-LoRA guide, so the model must generate motion and syncs the mouth to the supplied track. The lipdub IC-LoRA fails exactly there, because LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide reproduces every source frame and freezing the audio pins the mouth with it. The app-side question is therefore probably not "wire the lipdub graph" but "can the graph that already does both audio modes take a video instead of a start frame", which may retire this card approach for the feature he wants.

Phase 4 done: the lipdub graph now carries the Input_*/Output_* title law - Input_Video, Input_Audio, Input_Positive, Input_Negative, Input_Seed, Output_Video. Two of the six are node SWAPS rather than renames, which the plan did not anticipate: MpiLoadVideo has no VIDEO output and emits images/audio/fps directly, so it replaces BOTH LoadVideo #5002 and GetVideoComponents #5010, and MpiSaveVideo takes images/audio/fps, so it replaces BOTH CreateVideo #4849 and SaveVideo #4852. With the three bypassed Gemma-API nodes dropped the graph is 35 nodes / 48 links, converting against 48188 to 33 API nodes with 0 unknown, 0 missing required, 0 dangling and nothing unreachable. The two loader substitutions are now BAKED IN - the first queue attempt returned the same 400 prompt_outputs_failed_validation Phase 1 recorded, because the template still named weights this install does not have. Proven equivalent, not merely runnable: re-ran the refvoice_tiny settings (same clip, voice, line and seed 43) as prompt 4b40f840-ae76-4317-8bc3-80ed5fb3d978, status success, 107.5s, output lipdub_phase4_00001.mp4 at 73x960x544 with both streams and the same -26.7 dB mean level; PSNR y 44.31 against the original with a flat 43.5-47.1 spread, the gap explained by MpiSaveVideo encoding at 1866 kb/s against 1043. A diff of the two dispatched graphs off /history shows 24 shared nodes with byte-identical scalar inputs, including the sampler, sigmas, CFG guider, IC-LoRA guide and all four loaders; the only three that differ do so because their literal now arrives over a link from the new Input_* node. Bench and repo copies byte-identical at 6b5a6f790fad4315.

Phase 4 ticked - Input_*/Output_* title law applied, three bypassed Gemma-API nodes dropped, loaders baked. Phase 5 (Fabio's judgement on lipdub_2stage_00001_ and appi2v_lipsync_00001) is the only phase left.

Fabio judged three outputs. Phase 4 PASSES - lipdub_phase4_00001.mp4 reproduces refvoice_tiny, so the title law costs nothing. TWO-STAGE IS OUT: lipdub_2stage_00001_ holds the face and the mouth does not move, and the dispatched graph names why - stage 2's LTXVConcatAVLatent takes its audio_latent from LTXVSetAudioRefTokens slot 2, which is frozen_audio, fed stage 1's separated audio latent, while LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide at strength 1.0 re-synthesises the video. That is exactly the configuration already proven dead at guide 1.00/0.75/0.50, so it is a wiring impossibility rather than a tuning problem; if 1920x1088 is wanted, upscale the DECODED stage-1 video through the app's existing upscale path instead. appi2v_lipsync_00001 also showed no mouth movement, and Fabio's read is that the prompt has to state she says something - the dispatched Input_Positive said she was talking to the camera but never gave her a line, while every working lipdub run carried the dialogue explicitly. Tested it: re-dispatched the same graph with only Input_Positive changed (prompt 961e6779, 126.3s, appi2v_speak_00001.mp4). PSNR y 20.41 against the no-dialogue run - against 44.31 for a known-identical generation - so the line is not a no-op and materially changed the output. Whether it produced lip motion needs Fabio's eye.

BREAKTHROUGH, judged by Fabio: appi2v_512_00001.mp4 has GOOD LIP SYNC from a supplied audio track, on ltx_i2v_t2v_template.json exactly as it ships - no lipdub IC-LoRA, no talking-head LoRA, no new node. That closes the singing case and confirms the reframe that the capability already ships and the gap is a video input. Two conditions had to be met, both missing from the earlier appi2v_lipsync attempt that read as a failure: the prompt must carry the spoken line (adding it moved the output by PSNR y 20.41 on a fixed seed, against 44.31 for an identical generation), and Input_Height must be divisible by 64 - the graph halves it at #156 MpiMath floor(a/2) and the latent then floors to a multiple of 32, so 544 became 512 while ImageResizeKJv2 sized the conditioning image to the injected 544, leaving the image 32px taller than the latent it conditioned. The 'different woman' complaint was neither of these: frame 0 of lipdub_face.mp4 is the BACK OF HER HEAD, so the model was handed no face and invented one, and faithfully continued the turn - diagnosed by looking at the frame rather than trusting the earlier session's label. The start frame must SHOW the face, which extends the face-size finding. On Fabio's question about elix3r/LTX-2.3-22b-AV-LoRA-talking-head: never tried, and not what this needs - it is a 428MB subject LoRA for one identity (trigger OHWXPERSON, 26 clips), a different file from the 1.16GB ltx-2.3-id-lora-talkvid-3k on disk, its lips follow GENERATED audio so it does not serve the singing case, and its licence forbids commercial use. Its README is valuable though: their training clips are made with BASE LTX-2.3 and no LoRA via LTX-2-3-I2V-Custom-Audio.json, whose audio path is identical to ours, and it documents 1280x704 @ 25fps for image+audio, a mouth-behaviour prompt block, and that simple dark backgrounds improve lip sync.

Identity confirmed preserved once the start frame shows the face. Re-ran the app i2v graph changing only the start frame to frame 64 of lipdub_face.mp4 (front-on, largest face), cropped to 960x512: prompt 7fe7d452, status success, 71.0s, appi2v_face64_00001.mp4. Frame 0 of the output is unmistakably the source character. Note for anyone repeating this: PSNR scored this correct run 20.26 against its conditioning image, LOWER than the wrong-woman run's 23.52, because the camera pushed in and the hair moved - a pixel metric measures framing, not identity, and reading it as identity would have manufactured a bug that does not exist. The question was settled by opening the frame.

Fabio's closing verdict. appi2v_face64_00001.mp4 held identity but the mouth did not move, and his read is SEED - he has seen specific seeds refuse to move the mouth on earlier image-to-video tests, and the elix3r model card independently lists seed-dependent output quality as a known limitation. That retires the i2v thread for this card on his direct statement: image-to-video with an audio track already works in the shipped app across multiple characters, including two voices in one file, so it was never the missing piece. The missing piece was the VIDEO-in front end, which is exactly this card's lipdub graph, and he judged the Phase 4 generation as working well. Correction recorded against the earlier two-stage verdict: it was n=1, and since seeds are now known to kill mouth motion on their own, that single observation cannot carry the conclusion by itself - the frozen_audio wiring argument still stands, but any revisit must sweep seeds. Two-stage stays out for v1 regardless: 3x the time, and the resolution is available by upscaling the decoded stage-1 video through the app's existing path. All five phases complete; the card's user-ux verify mode is satisfied by Fabio's own judgement.
doing -> done. Bench authoring complete and user-verified: the lipdub graph is authored, proven, retitled to the Input_*/Output_* injection contract, and judged working by Fabio.
